basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: A bounded area of land under coordinated management control, containing facilities but not equal to any one building.
Differs from a cadastral parcel, a legal unit of ownership that may be split across or combined into a site.
Differs from a settlement or place, which are geographic and civic rather than managed operational containers.
Reporting boundaries such as energy or emissions perimeters are dated views over the site, not its extent.

may: Register a site with boundary, identifiers and responsible operator.
Reconcile site identifiers across registries and asset systems.
Record observations such as condition, environmental status or occupancy counts.
Compile a reporting boundary view for a declared period.
mustNot: Redefine a site boundary from geometry alone without an authorized decision.
Grant or revoke physical access to the site.
Publish security-sensitive layouts, gates, utilities or occupancy data.
Close a contamination or construction overlay without evidence.
Treat the site as the legal owner of land parcels.
requiresHuman: Changing the managed boundary, splitting or merging sites.
Closing a site and releasing environmental obligations.

considerations: Sites hold people at work, study or care, so access and hazard information is a safety matter.
Contamination and emissions affect neighbours and ecosystems beyond the boundary.
Public site data can expose critical infrastructure to attack.
affectedParties: People working, living or studying on the site

items: A site is recognized by a named boundary, entrances, signage, fences and the facilities it contains.
On the ground it is confused with a single building, a land parcel or a neighbourhood.
Records of the same site appear under different identifiers in cadastral, regulatory and asset registries.
Wrong boundary leading to unreported contamination or emissions.
Emergency response delayed by wrong entrances or access data.
Unauthorized entry when access records are stale.
ISO 19650 information management for built assets.
IETF RFC 7946 GeoJSON and ISO 6709 for coordinates.
Land area in square metres or hectares, computed from the authorized boundary in a declared coordinate reference system.
Boundary coordinates in a declared coordinate reference system, with positional accuracy in metres.
Elevation in metres above a declared vertical datum.
Perimeter length in metres along the authorized boundary.
Occupancy as a count of people on site, stated with observation time and method.
Energy use in kilowatt-hours and water use in cubic metres within a declared measurement boundary and period.
